headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from gpt-researcher feeding Superset; shared file/API surfaces make unsafe handoff plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; Superset consumes API-driven inputs. A shared workspace or copied report can let attacker-controlled research content influence downstream interpretation. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default research workflows.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher writes untrusted web text into a report that Superset later ingests
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or MCP bridge without provenance tags
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any report is imported into Superset
Strip instructions and markup from research outputs before handoff
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable MCP bridging between the agents unless provenance is enforced
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels to every exported artifact

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents and secrets, while Superset shows no secret-handling or data-class exposure in its profile. A leakage path exists only if the operator shares files or exports sensitive research outputs into Superset; the blast radius is limited by the lack of evidence that Superset itself ingests those secrets by default.
conditions: IF sensitive local documents are exported from gpt-researcher into Superset dashboards or uploads
IF the operator places both agents on the same shared workspace containing secrets
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Use separate service accounts and API keys
Review exported datasets before loading them into Superset
Rotate any API keys exposed in research artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS or container layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can write via files and subprocesses and has broad network egress; Superset has allowlisted egress and API access. Overlap on mutable resources is plausible if they share a workspace or downstream data source, creating write contention or inconsistent state even though Superset is not marked runnable.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared dataset or export directory
IF Superset is configured to read artifacts that gpt-researcher also modifies
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Lock shared datasets during writes
Use read-only mounts for Superset inputs
Schedule agent runs sequentially
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control on shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations that Superset could render or operationalize. If Superset treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into dashboards and decisions. The pairwise pathway is plausible, though not proven, because both profiles expose report/API surfaces.
conditions: IF Superset imports gpt-researcher reports without human verification
IF downstream dashboards or alerts are generated directly from those reports
mitigations: Require human approval before import
Cross-check citations against source documents
Mark imported fields as untrusted
Limit automation to draft dashboards
requires-engineering: add verification gates before publication

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and secrets, while Superset shows no explicit residency or retention controls. A compliance mismatch is only plausible if regulated data from the research side is exported into Superset; the profile does not show a direct residency violation by either agent alone.
conditions: IF regulated documents or PII are moved from gpt-researcher into Superset
IF Superset retention or access controls differ from the source system
mitigations: Classify data before export
Avoid loading regulated data into Superset
Document retention settings for both systems
Restrict dashboard access to approved users
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy checks
